- Overestimate prices after sentiment spikes (especially when sentiment > 0.5) — model tends to overshoot and then correct.
- Underestimate when sentiment is low or negative (sentiment < 0.3) — model fails to capture downward pressure.
- Lag in price correction: model often lags 1–3 days behind true price movements, especially after sharp spikes.
- Mean reversion bias: model overreacts to short-term volatility, underestimating long-term trend reversion.
- Horizon-specific error: 30-day forecasts consistently overestimate by 0.5–2.5% in early cycles, then converge — adjust for diminishing forecast error as horizon approaches 30 days.
- Sentiment-weighted adjustment: if sentiment > 0.6, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overconfidence; if sentiment < 0.3, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to account for underreaction.
